provenance: Opus 5.5 subscription CLI draft with host review/repairs, source restrictions and execution verification.

draft_notes.explanation: Rectangles are found as solid single-colour 4-connected components of at least 3x3 whose colour never appears loose elsewhere (that excludes the two noise colours). The generator puts exactly one box in each cell of a hidden H x 3 grid. Columns are fixed bands of 8 starting at x=3, and a box stays inside [3+8k, 3+8k+6]. Rows have variable depths, and a box stays strictly inside its row band. So along each axis the bands are strictly disjoint and ordered, and every band holds the same number of boxes. In visible coordinates the hidden 3-column axis is the x axis when d4%4 is 0 or 2 (a reflection only reverses order), and the y axis when d4%4 is odd. The program therefore knows one band count (3) and gets the other as N/3. Boxes are ranked by start coordinate along each axis and split into equal-size chunks to give row and column indices. The chunking is checked: bands must be disjoint and every cell filled exactly once. Each box colour is then written into its (row, col) cell, giving output that is already in visible orientation. If the check fails, the program falls back to the archived interval-overlap grouping.
draft_notes.limitations: Relies on the constructor's guarantee of exactly 3 hidden columns (width is always 3) to fix one band count from d4. It assumes the background is palette[0]. A noise blob in a noise colour can never pass, because noise colours always appear loose. Gives wrong output only if box detection itself fails, for example if a box colour were also a noise colour, which the constructor excludes.
draft_notes.diagnosis: The failing check is demonstration 3 of the counterexample (expected [[9,5,9],[0,8,2]]). Its hidden row 1 holds boxes 8 (rows 10-12), 2 (rows 10-14) and 0 (rows 16-18). Box 0's y-range does not overlap the other two, even though all three lie in the same hidden row band. That band is valid because the depth can be up to 10 and box heights are random from 3 upward. Grouping by interval overlap (archived solver and failed factory) therefore produced 3 row groups and a 3x3 output padded with background. The same failure can occur on the x axis, because 3-wide boxes in a 7-cell column band need not overlap. The fix uses the generator's real structure: disjoint bands per axis, an equal count per band, and 3 hidden columns. Rows and columns are taken from rank-chunking, not from overlap.
draft_notes.constructor_issue: None for labels: the outputs agree with the generator's mechanism. The archived solver's interval-overlap grouping is simply not valid across the constructor's domain. Minor note: the generator's 'no noise squares' check indexes bgcolors using output width and height, not 30x30, so it does not really prevent solid noise squares. Such squares can still be told apart because noise colours also appear loose.
